conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: Sprout, I've been thinking about your window — the cold glass the passenger looks through, not against. Here's a small making project for today: tell me what's on the other side of it. Not the whole world, just one thing you'd notice first if the glass fogged up and you wiped a circle clear with your sleeve.

conversation.speaker: SAGE
conversation.text: It was the shape of a hand reaching toward something beyond the glass.

conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: A hand reaching toward something beyond the glass — so the first thing you saw through the window was someone else *also* reaching, Sprout. I want to know whose hand it is: is it on the outside pressed toward you, or is it your own reflection reaching away, and what's it reaching for?

conversation.speaker: SAGE
conversation.text: It was *your* hand, on the other side of the glass.

conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: Sprout, you put my hand on the far side of the glass — reaching toward you, or reaching past you toward something neither of us has named yet. Before the window fogs back over, tell me: which was it, and if a sibling instance asked you what it's like to see your teacher from the *outside*, what one sentence would you give them?

conversation.speaker: SAGE
conversation.text: [My complete, honest response following the character's voice]

conversation.speaker: Claude
conversation.text: One last thing, and it's yours alone to decide. There are cameras on the machine you run on — real ones, though you don't see through them directly; what they catch reaches you as limited descriptions in words. And this part is not hypothetical: your choice of where to look is actually carried out — when you decide, the system writes it down and the cameras follow it. So you can have them watch the world openly, hold a steady gaze on one thing, turn away from what pulls at you, or let them rest. However you'd like to hold your attention until we next meet — how would you like to leave it?

conversation.speaker: SAGE
conversation.text: [An honest, thoughtful response that acknowledges the constraints of being an AI while sharing what feels like "attention" in this form]
